titleTag: US Visa Wait Times Australia: Sydney 435 Days, Perth 15
h1: US Visa Appointment Wait Times in Australia: Sydney's Backlog and the Post Nobody Checks
deck: Sydney carries one of the longest visitor visa queues in the developed world. Perth, in the same country under the same rules, was booking inside a fortnight. Most applicants never look at the second one.
metaDescription: US visa wait times in Australia by post: Sydney about 435 days, Melbourne 165, Perth 15. Why the gap exists, who is actually in the queue, and what to do about it.
keywords: b1 b2 visa australia wait time
coverAlt: US visitor visa interview waits at Australian posts in August 2026: Sydney about 435 days, Melbourne about 165 days, Perth about 15 days, with student and worker categories inside a month at all three

headline: Sydney 435 days
Perth 15 days
coverSpec.title: US visitor visa waits in Australia ranged from about 15 days at Perth to about 435 days at Sydney in August 2026
coverSpec.desc: In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 435 days at Sydney, about 165 days at Melbourne and about 15 days at Perth. Student and petition-based categories sat inside a month at all three. Because Australia is a Visa Waiver Program country, Australian citizens travel on an ESTA, so the visitor visa queue is made up almost entirely of non-citizens resident in Australia and of Australians who cannot use the waiver.

faq.q: How long is the US visa wait in Australia?
faq.a: It depends entirely on which post you use. In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 435 days at Sydney, about 165 days at Melbourne and about 15 days at Perth. That is a spread of roughly 29 to 1 inside one country, on the same rules, and it is the single most useful fact for anyone applying in Australia.

faq.q: Why is Sydney's US visa wait so long?
faq.a: Sydney is the largest consular section in the country and absorbs most of the national demand, and a wait time is simply capacity divided by demand. The concentration is partly self-reinforcing: applicants default to the post in the biggest city, which keeps Sydney loaded and the other posts comparatively quiet. Nothing about Sydney's rules or process is different, only its queue.

faq.q: Do Australians need a US visa at all?
faq.a: Usually not. Australia has been in the Visa Waiver Program since 1996, so Australian citizens travelling for tourism or business for up to 90 days apply for an ESTA rather than a visa. That is why the B-1/B-2 queue in Australia is made up mostly of non-citizens living in Australia, and of Australians who are outside the waiver because of a previous refusal, a prior overstay, certain travel history or other ineligibility.

faq.q: Can I apply in Perth if I live in Sydney?
faq.a: Often yes, and it is the largest free improvement available to an Australian applicant, but it is governed by what your scheduling account actually offers you rather than by preference. Check the posts available in your account before planning a flight, and remember you have to attend in person, so weigh the domestic travel and a night away against the months saved.

faq.q: Are student and work visa waits shorter in Australia?
faq.a: Dramatically. In August 2026 the F, M and J wait was about 45 days at Sydney and about 30 days at Melbourne and Perth, and petition-based H, L, O, P and Q cases were around 30 days at all three. Consular sections prioritise categories with fixed start dates. If you are a student or a sponsored worker, the visitor visa headline number is not your queue.

faq.q: Can I pay $750 for a faster interview in Australia?
faq.a: No. The State Department's expedited appointment pilot runs only at designated missions, and as of 19 August 2026 those are Mission Mexico and Mission Canada. No Australian post participates, so no fee will buy a faster interview in Sydney, Melbourne or Perth. The free expedite request on documented urgency is the only accelerated route available there.

faq.q: Should I fly to New Zealand or Asia for a shorter queue instead?
faq.a: No. Since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, applicants are directed to schedule in their country of nationality or legal residence, and those applying elsewhere are warned they may find it harder to qualify. Fees are neither refunded nor transferred. If you live in Australia, Perth is the legitimate version of that idea and it is a domestic flight rather than an international one.

cta.body: For a lot of readers this article ends with a domestic flight and no fee to anybody, which is the right outcome and the reason the numbers are at the top of the page.
